title: Operation Sindoor Turns One: PM Modi Leads National Tribute, IAF Releases Unseen Strike Footage, MEA Reaffirms Anti-Terror Doctrine
detail: On May 7, 2026 — the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor — India mounted a coordinated national commemoration marking the May 7, 2025 precision strikes on nine Pakistan-based terror infrastructure targets. Prime Minister Narendra Modi changed his profile picture on X, Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp to an 'Operation Sindoor' tribute graphic, posting: 'A year ago, our armed forces displayed unparalleled courage, precision and resolve during #OperationSindoor. They gave a fitting response to those who dared to attack innocent Indians at Pahalgam. Today, a year later, we remain as steadfast as ever in our resolve to defeat terrorism and destroy its enabling ecosystem.' Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, and the full Cabinet joined the social media tribute. The Indian Air Force (IAF) released exclusively timed, previously unseen footage from the May 7, 2025 strikes — timed to mirror the exact hour the operation launched (approximately 1:05 AM) — showing BrahMos cruise missile strikes, destroyed Pakistani radar systems, and collapsed hangars. India's Ministry of External Affairs issued a formal statement: 'India has every right to defend itself against cross-border terrorism.' Senior military commanders, including former DGMO Lt Gen Rajiv Ghai, held media briefings. Analysts across Indian media — The Week, BusinessToday, Open the Magazine — published major long-form analyses marking the 'doctrinal shift' established by Sindoor: India no longer distinguishes between terrorist perpetrators and their state sponsors, and any future attack will be treated as an act of war — a transition from 'strategic restraint' to 'strategic proactiveness.' The Washington Post and The Diplomat published anniversary assessments describing the ceasefire as 'holding, so far' while warning of elevated escalation dynamics. The bilateral freeze remains unchanged: airspace closed until May 24, Indus Waters Treaty suspended, all trade halted, no ambassadors exchanged.

media.caption: PM Modi leads Operation Sindoor first anniversary commemoration — changes profile pictures on all social media platforms; IAF releases previously unseen strike footage (May 7, 2026)

title: DG ISPR Chaudhry Holds Marka-e-Haq Anniversary Press Conference: 'Pakistan Proved Strength Against 5× Bigger Enemy — Any Hostile Design Will Be Countered With Greater Force'
detail: On May 7, 2026 — the first anniversary of Marka-e-Haq (Pakistan's name for the May 7–10, 2025 conflict) — Pakistan's DG ISPR Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry held a major press conference at ISPR headquarters attended by senior tri-service representation, including Deputy Chief of Naval Staff (Operations) Rear Admiral Shifaat Ali Khan and Deputy Chief of Air Staff (Projects) Air Vice Marshal Tariq Mahmood Ghazi. Key DG ISPR statements: (1) 'Pakistan proved its strength against a 5-times bigger enemy in Marka-e-Haq'; (2) India's attempt to paint Pakistan as a state sponsor of terrorism had been 'buried forever'; (3) Pakistan has emerged as the 'biggest ambassador of regional security, crushing India's terror nation rhetoric'; (4) The Pakistan Air Force's performance in the conflict 'will be inscribed in golden letters of history'; (5) Pakistan's Armed Forces formally vowed that any 'hostile design' against Pakistan would be countered with 'greater strength, precision and resolve' than India saw in May 2025. The DG ISPR press conference — flanked by naval and air force senior officers — represents Pakistan's highest-profile military anniversary statement, with the tri-service format designed to project unified deterrence. The warning of 'greater strength' directly responds to India's own anniversary messaging and Rajnath Singh's 'voluntary halt' narrative, establishing Pakistan's counter-narrative that India was compelled to stop rather than chose to. Pakistan's media — ARY News, Geo TV, Daily Pakistan — broadcast the presser live. The conference took place as India simultaneously released IAF strike footage and PM Modi issued his anniversary tribute.

media.caption: DG ISPR Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry at Marka-e-Haq anniversary press conference (May 7, 2026), flanked by Deputy Chiefs of Navy and Air Force — warns India of 'greater strength' in any future conflict
